verdicts.claim: UXP does not exist in any shipping After Effects release as of 2026-10-02. The AE UXP public beta is promised for November 2026 with no GA date. The early-preview AE UXP docs (AdobeDocs/uxp-after-effects PR #10, 2026-09-29) tag every host API member 'Min Version 27.0' / 'Since 27.0'. The current release is 26.5 and AE (Beta) is on 27.0. Adobe staff (Erin Finnegan, March 2026) gave the order Premiere -> AME -> AE and advised against a complicated CEP UI.
evidence: Adobe developer blog, Sept 2026 (https://blog.developer.adobe.com/en/publish/2026/09/investing-in-the-future-of-creative-cloud-extensibility-uxp-comes-to-our-flagship-applications), raw text saved to scratchpad/work/fc/blog_uxp_2026_09.txt: After Effects gets public-beta UXP plugins 'by November 2026'. No GA date. Media Encoder's public beta is live and Premiere is GA with Hybrid plugins.

GitHub API: AdobeDocs/uxp-after-effects was created 2026-09-23. PR #10 'Publish early-preview After Effects UXP documentation' was merged 2026-09-29. src/pages/site-wide-banner.json describes the docs as an early preview that is still being updated (https://github.com/AdobeDocs/uxp-after-effects/pull/10).

I downloaded all 44 AE API pages from the repo and counted the tags: 532 'Since: 27.0' tags and 940 Min Version table cells, every one 27.0, none lower. The Get Started page is an empty stub. No page mentions WebView or Hybrid plugins (https://github.com/AdobeDocs/uxp-after-effects/tree/main/src/pages/after-effects-api).
Helpx AE release notes, last updated 2026-09-09: the latest version is the September 2026 release, 26.5 (https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/what-s-new/release-notes-after-effects.html).
Adobe community announcement, 2026-08-06, features 'After Effects Beta 27.0 Build 6 and later' (https://community.adobe.com/announcements-532/new-in-beta-contour-paint-effect-1635333).
The Bolt UXP README lists After Effects (Beta) and says it needs beta access from Adobe app teams (https://github.com/hyperbrew/bolt-uxp#supported-adobe-apps).

Forum thread 11777 (https://forums.creativeclouddeveloper.com/t/when-will-uxp-come-to-after-effect/11777), Erin Finnegan (staff). On 2026-03-12 she gave the order Premiere -> AME -> AE. On 2026-03-17 she said she would not necessarily wait, pointed to scripts or C++ plug-ins, and advised against a very complicated CEP UI. She added that an experienced developer in a hurry could still build one.

The AE UXP docs list more binding differences than the research does. AVLayer/TextLayer.addToMotionGraphicsTemplate emits a warning and returns undefined instead of false on failure (scratchpad/work/fc/aeuxp/after-effects-api__avlayer.md).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed. Three refinements. (1) Adobe's wording is 'by November 2026', a deadline rather than a date. (2) Finnegan's caution was qualified: experienced developers in a hurry could still build a CEP UI. Her 'don't wait' advice pointed to scripts and C++ plug-ins, not CEP. (3) The 27.0 UXP binding has more documented differences from ExtendScript than setParentWithJump and render(skipCheck), for example add-to-EGP returning undefined. The port is close to mechanical, not fully mechanical.

verdicts.claim: CEP is fully supported in AE 2025 and 2026 (CEP 12: Chromium 99, Node 17.7.1, NW 0.62.1, CSXS.12). Adobe's Sept 2026 timeline for AE: Marketplace stops new CEP submissions and CEP is disabled by default from December 2028 (users can re-enable). CEP is removed from new versions from December 2029, with at least two years after the UXP beta. 'CEP plugins distributed outside the Marketplace are not affected by this milestone.'
evidence: CEP 12 HTML Extension Cookbook (https://github.com/Adobe-CEP/CEP-Resources/blob/master/CEP_12.x/Documentation/CEP%2012%20HTML%20Extension%20Cookbook.md): PPRO 25.0 and AEFT 25.0 use CEP 12. Chromium 99, Node.js 17.7.1, Node-WebKit 0.62.1. PlayerDebugMode lives under HKCU/Software/Adobe/CSXS.12.
Adobe-CEP/CEP-Resources has no CEP_13.x folder. The latest commit is 2026-02-20, so AE 26.x still ships CEP 12.

Blog text (https://blog.developer.adobe.com/en/publish/2026/09/investing-in-the-future-of-creative-cloud-extensibility-uxp-comes-to-our-flagship-applications): AE, Illustrator and AME stop new CEP submissions and become CEP-disabled-by-default together in December 2028. Users can easily turn CEP back on. From December 2029 CEP is no longer included. Until then, existing Marketplace plugins keep working and can be updated. Each app gets at least two years after its UXP public beta.

The sentence saying off-Marketplace CEP plugins are 'not affected by this milestone' sits in the blog's Photoshop March 2027 Marketplace-submission section. It covers only Marketplace submission cutoffs, not disabled-by-default or removal.
The same blog says CEP no longer works reliably and will be retired at the end of 2029.

Helpx fixed issues, 25.6: scripts, ScriptUI panels and CEP extensions no longer load in Safe Mode. CEP is still being maintained in AE (https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/troubleshooting/fixed-and-known-issues/fixed-issues.html).

Secondary sources show CEP 12 panels running on AE 26.3 and 26.5 (https://github.com/Engine-Room-Games/after-effects-mcp/issues/91, https://github.com/leancoderkavy/premiere-pro-mcp/issues/504). Issue #91 is also a third-party report that PlayerDebugMode was ignored on one Windows AE 26.3 machine until the panel was self-signed.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed. The 'not affected' exemption applies only to Marketplace submission cutoffs (AE December 2028, Premiere December 2027). An internally distributed ZXP is still disabled by default in AE and Premiere from December 2028, so users must re-enable CEP. It is also absent from versions released from December 2029. Adobe itself calls CEP unreliable, so treat CEP 12 as a bridge, not a long-term base.

verdicts.claim: ExtendScript in After Effects is not being retired. AE keeps adding ExtendScript APIs in 26.0, 26.3 and 26.5. The vault note 'ExtendScript EOL September 2026' misreads Premiere-only statements: the scripting guide's 'through September 2026' and PProPanel's 'calendar year'. Both are superseded by the September 2026 timeline. Premiere's ExtendScript API has been frozen since PPro 23.0.
evidence: Adobe blog, Sept 2026: ExtendScripts are not affected by the CEP-to-UXP transition (https://blog.developer.adobe.com/en/publish/2026/09/investing-in-the-future-of-creative-cloud-extensibility-uxp-comes-to-our-flagship-applications).
Adobe staff bbb_999 in the Developers Live Q&A, 2026-09-29: "We also have no plans to remove ExtendScript, from Pr / Ae / AME." (https://forums.creativeclouddeveloper.com/t/12215)

AE scripting guide changelog: 26.0 (January 2026) added addVariableFontAxis, propertyParameters and valueText. 26.3 (June 2026) added ParametricMeshLayer. 26.5 (September 2026) added GuideOptions and the layer input-stage APIs. Repo last pushed 2026-09-11 (https://github.com/docsforadobe/after-effects-scripting-guide/blob/master/docs/introduction/changelog.md).

The Premiere scripting guide index says Premiere moved to UXP as of November 2025 and ExtendScript is supported through September 2026. Its changelog records the 23.0 decision that no further ExtendScript API changes are planned. The repo has not been updated since 2025-11-11 (https://github.com/docsforadobe/premiere-scripting-guide).

The PProPanel README was last updated in November 2025 for 25.6 (commit 2025-11-11). It states the plan to support CEP and UXP for a calendar year and then remove CEP (https://github.com/Adobe-CEP/Samples/blob/master/PProPanel/ReadMe.md).
bbb_999, 2026-06-22: Adobe has no plans to build any bridge from UXP to ExtendScript (https://forums.creativeclouddeveloper.com/t/11408).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed and strengthened. On 2026-09-29 Adobe staff said there are no plans to remove ExtendScript from Premiere, AE or AME, which covers the now-expired 'through September 2026' wording in the Premiere guide. The vault notes should be corrected. Caveat: Adobe will not provide a UXP-to-ExtendScript bridge, so ExtendScript code cannot be called from a future UXP plugin and must be ported.

verdicts.claim: Premiere UXP is GA since 25.6 (beta 25.2 on 2024-12-04, Hybrid in 26.2, API v26.5). The calls a brand panel needs exist in both stacks: insertMogrtFromPath, insertMogrtFromLibrary, getInstalledMogrtPath, importAEComps, importAllAEComps and importFiles in UXP; importMGT, getMGTComponent and importAEComps in ExtendScript. So the Premiere adapter maps one-to-one to UXP (getMGTComponent -> component params).
evidence: The version facts are correct per the Premiere UXP changelog: 25.2 initial public beta on 2024-12-04, 25.6 official release, 26.2 Hybrid plugins, 26.5 latest (https://github.com/AdobeDocs/uxp-premiere-pro/blob/main/src/pages/changelog/index.md).

The API names are correct. SequenceEditor.insertMogrtFromPath(inMGTPath, inTime, inVideoTrackIndex, inAudioTrackIndex), insertMogrtFromLibrary and getInstalledMogrtPath are all Since 25.6. So are Project.importAEComps(aepPath, compNames, targetBin), importAllAEComps and importFiles (https://github.com/AdobeDocs/uxp-premiere-pro/blob/main/src/pages/ppro-reference/classes/sequenceeditor.md, .../classes/project.md).

Forum thread 'MOGRT Parameters in UXP availability' (2025-09 to 2026-09): developers cannot read or set MOGRT text fields or 'Graphic Parameters' values through Premiere UXP; they get null or unsupported-type results. Dropdowns are partly settable (https://forums.creativeclouddeveloper.com/t/11408).

In the same thread, Adobe staff (bbb_999): on 2026-04-29 he acknowledged the MOGRT component shortcoming. On 2026-06-22 he said the work is underway with no date. On 2026-09-25 he gave CEP+ExtendScript to UXP parity by the end of calendar 2026 as a goal.

Developers Live Q&A, 2026-09-29: a developer states UXP cannot read or write Source Text of Premiere titles. Adobe puts native text-layer creation on its post-parity list (https://forums.creativeclouddeveloper.com/t/12228).
The Premiere UXP changelog through 26.5 has no MOGRT-parameter entry. 26.5 fixed importAEComps/importAllAEComps resolving true without importing anything when no targetBin was passed.

ExtendScript side exists: Sequence.importMGT(path, ticks, vidTrackOffset, audTrackOffset), TrackItem.getMGTComponent() and Project.importAEComps(path, compNames, targetBin) (https://github.com/docsforadobe/premiere-scripting-guide).
verdicts.corrected_claim: The version history and the insert/import call names are correct. The parity claim is false for the operation the brand panel most needs in Premiere: setting a MOGRT's text and brand parameters after insertion. That works in ExtendScript via getMGTComponent but has no working UXP equivalent as of Premiere 26.5 (late September 2026). Adobe targets parity by the end of 2026 with no committed date. The Premiere adapter is therefore not one-to-one today, and a 2027 Premiere UXP port is blocked until MOGRT component params ship. Always pass an explicit targetBin to UXP importAEComps.

verdicts.claim: The vault note 'MOGRT via ExtendScript is technically impossible' is false. The API exists since AE 15.0 (motionGraphicsTemplateName, exportAsMotionGraphicsTemplate, openInEssentialGraphics, Property.add/canAddToMotionGraphicsTemplate), with 15.1 (return-value fix), 16.1 (addToMotionGraphicsTemplateAs, controller names), 18.0 (media replacement) and 22.0 (essentialPropertySource). Commercial scripts (Aep to Mogrt Pro 2.1.3) automate it. The September 2026 report premiere-pro-mcp #504 was caused only by the missing comp argument and fixed by commit d8ff2a1.
evidence: AE scripting guide: CompItem.motionGraphicsTemplateName, exportAsMotionGraphicsTemplate and openInEssentialGraphics were added in 15.0. 15.1 fixed exportAsMotionGraphicsTemplate not returning a boolean. 16.1 added controller count, name getter and setter, and addToMotionGraphicsTemplateAs. 18.0 added AVLayer.add/canAddToMotionGraphicsTemplate, alternateSource and setAlternateSource. 22.0 added essentialPropertySource (https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/introduction/changelog/, /item/compitem/, /property/property/, /layer/avlayer/).

Adobe's own AE UXP 27.0 reference documents the same MOGRT methods on CompItem, Property and the layer classes (https://github.com/AdobeDocs/uxp-after-effects/blob/main/src/pages/after-effects-api/compitem.md).

aescripts product page: Aep to Mogrt Pro 2.1.3, released 2026-04-30, supports AE CC 2017 through 2026. It batch-adds properties and media replacement to the EGP, batch-exports .mogrt files and injects previews. Its 2.1.3 fix is to open comps in Essential Graphics before export (https://aescripts.com/aep-to-mogrt/).

Adobe bug thread: users exported MOGRTs by script on AE 23.x to 25.1; only the return value was wrong (https://community.adobe.com/bug-reports-528/after-effects-24-2-1-exportasmotiongraphicstemplate-not-returning-correct-value-1217054).

premiere-pro-mcp #504 (AE 26.5, Windows, 2026-09-14) describes two bugs. Bug 1 was an argument-count crash, fixed by passing comp. Bug 2 is that after the fix, canAddToMotionGraphicsTemplate(comp) still returned false for every property (text, color), so nothing was exposed. The reporter tried openInViewer but never openInEssentialGraphics. PR #507 (https://github.com/leancoderkavy/premiere-pro-mcp/pull/507) only addresses Bug 1, and the issue was closed without resolving Bug 2 (https://github.com/leancoderkavy/premiere-pro-mcp/issues/504).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed: scripted MOGRT authoring and export has been in the API since AE 15.0, Adobe documents it again in the 27.0 UXP binding, and a commercial tool supports AE 2026. One correction: #504 was not only the missing comp argument. After passing comp, the reporter still could not expose any property on AE 26.5 in a headless run without openInEssentialGraphics, and that is unresolved. Headless EGP exposure on 26.5 is probably viable with openInEssentialGraphics first, but stays unverified until a spike.

verdicts.claim: MOGRT scripting limits: (a) unsaved changes trigger a save prompt, so call save() first; (b) since 24.1/24.2.1 exportAsMotionGraphicsTemplate() returns false before export finishes, Adobe reproduced it in February 2024, it was still open in February 2025, and no fix appears up to 26.5; (c) call openInEssentialGraphics first; (d) poster time, groups, comments, Source Text font controls and the video-preview/compatibility options are not scriptable; (e) documented types are Checkbox, Color, Slider and Source Text; (f) MOGRT content rules apply.
evidence: The scripting guide and the AE UXP docs both say AE prompts to save if the project changed since the last save, and recommend calling save() before exporting (https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/item/compitem/).

Bug thread (https://community.adobe.com/bug-reports-528/after-effects-24-2-1-exportasmotiongraphicstemplate-not-returning-correct-value-1217054): reported 2024-02-23 for 24.2.1 and 24.1.x. AE Engineering (John Colombo) reproduced it on 2024-05-03, not in February 2024. Kevin Monahan (Adobe) said on 2025-02-04 it was still being worked on.

In the same thread, a user on 24.3 (Windows) and 25.1 (macOS) reports the call always returns false before the export completes, and that later export calls fail as a result. The original reporter also asked for scripting control over the 'include video previews' option.

Helpx fixed-issues page (17.x to 26.5), keyword scan: no fix for the export return value. Only unrelated EGP fixes appear: 26.5 Reveal in Timeline, 26.3 Open in Essential Graphics in Team Projects, 25.4 Adobe Clean font warnings on mogrt import (https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/troubleshooting/fixed-and-known-issues/fixed-issues.html).

canAddToMotionGraphicsTemplate docs list Checkbox, Color, single-value numerical slider and Source Text. AE shows a warning dialog when a property cannot be added, which is a modal interruption in batch runs (https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/property/property/).
I searched the full ExtendScript guide and the AE UXP 27.0 docs for poster time, EGP groups and comments, video preview and compatibility options: neither has any API for them.

Adobe bug thread, February 2025: Source Text Properties (font, style, size) can be overridden by script only if they were switched on in the EGP, and switching them on is not scriptable (https://community.adobe.com/bug-reports-528/24-2-1-bug-text-essential-prop-not-returning-override-value-1217063).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed, with three corrections. (1) Adobe reproduced the early-false return on 2024-05-03, not in February 2024, and it was still unfixed as of the 26.5 fixed-issues list. (2) Users report that starting a new export before the previous one finishes can fail, so run exports strictly one at a time and poll for a stable file. (3) add/canAddToMotionGraphicsTemplate raise a modal warning on failure, so call canAdd first. The Source Text font/size/style toggles cannot be enabled by script and must be set by hand when authoring the template.

verdicts.claim: Essential Properties (AE 15.1+) let nested instances override values. Scripts reach them through the precomp layer's 'ADBE Layer Overrides' group, then .property(i).setValue(). essentialPropertySource arrived in 22.0 and setAlternateSource in 18.0. AE 25.2 fixed reading the overridden Source Text value, and 26.3 fixed a replaceSource crash. So: import the .aep, add the primary comp at the playhead, set Essential Properties, and require AE 25.2+.
evidence: AVLayer match names: the top-level group 'ADBE Layer Overrides' = Essential Properties. The match name was added in the 18.0 changelog (https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/matchnames/layer/avlayer/).
The essentialPropertySource example (22.0) reads values with layer.essentialProperty.property(1) (https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/property/property/).

Helpx fixed issues, 25.2: scripting now returns the overridden Source Text essential-property value rather than the primary value. An Adobe Sr. Quality Engineer (Sébastien Périer) confirmed the fix shipped in 25.2 on 2025-04-02. Reads returned the primary value from 24.2.x to 25.1; writes worked (https://community.adobe.com/bug-reports-528/24-2-1-bug-text-essential-prop-not-returning-override-value-1217063).

Helpx fixed issues, 26.3: scripting replaceSource on a precomp shown in the Properties panel no longer crashes, and Essential Properties no longer open with incorrect values or flicker. 26.2: EP values are no longer shared across precomps in the same 3D bin with Advanced 3D and Collapse Transformations. 25.6: no crash when precomposing nested comps with many EPs (https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/troubleshooting/fixed-and-known-issues/fixed-issues.html).

An AE 2025 user thread confirms 'ADBE EP Text Document' inside 'ADBE Layer Overrides' is the access path, and that the 25.2 beta fixed it (https://community.adobe.com/questions-529/scripting-essential-properties-text-values-59210).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed. AE 25.2 is the hard minimum for correct Essential Property text reads. AE 26.2 and 26.3 fixed further EP bugs (wrong values on open, flicker, values shared across precomps under Advanced 3D, replaceSource crash), so make 26.3+ the tested and supported baseline while still allowing 25.2. Text overrides work. Font/size/style overrides work only if the template author enabled those Source Text properties in the EGP by hand.

verdicts.claim: One UI codebase for AE and Premiere is practical. Bolt CEP builds one multi-host CEP extension (Vite/TS, evalTS to ES3, ZXP signing, CC 2024+). Later, a UXP WebView (since UXP 6.0; local files since 8.0; WebView2 or WKWebView; webview.allow, allowLocalRendering, enableMessageBridge) can host the same web bundle. Bolt UXP has a WebView UI option and lists Premiere (GA) and AE (Beta). Native UXP lacks CSS Grid. Chromium 99 is the lowest common browser.
evidence: Bolt CEP README: multi-host-app configuration, evalTS() type-safe calls, ES6 compiled to one ES3 ExtendScript file, Adobe CC 2024 or later, special setup on Mac arm64. ZXPSignCmd broke on 2025-04-18 and Adobe fixed it on 2025-04-30 (https://github.com/hyperbrew/bolt-cep).
Premiere UXP CSS recipe: UXP does not support all CSS, and CSS Grid Layout is not available (https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/resources/recipes/css-styling/).

HTMLWebViewElement docs (https://developer.adobe.com/premiere-pro/uxp/uxp-api/reference-js/global-members/html-elements/html-web-view-element): the element exists since v6.0. Local content works from UXP 8.0 via allowLocalRendering. The manifest keys are allow, domains, allowLocalRendering and enableMessageBridge, and manifest v5+ is required. Windows errors map to WebView2. Adobe warns WebViews are resource-intensive and meant for cases plain UXP cannot handle.

UXP changelog in the Premiere docs: WebView for panels arrived in UXP 6.4, local HTML in 8.0, and Premiere support starts at UXP 8.1 (https://github.com/AdobeDocs/uxp-premiere-pro/blob/main/src/pages/uxp-api/changelog3-p.md).

Bolt UXP README: an opt-in WebView UI using Edge on Windows and Safari on macOS, a typed api bridge between the two contexts, multi-panel support. It lists Premiere Pro, and After Effects (Beta) only with Adobe beta access (https://github.com/hyperbrew/bolt-uxp).
Adobe's September 2026 blog says WebView and Hybrid plugins help bridge architecture differences during migration.
The AE UXP preview docs say nothing about WebView. A Hyper Brew 'Champion' (not Adobe) recommends a WebView UI for full DOM support in AE UXP (https://forums.creativeclouddeveloper.com/t/12224).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed for Premiere. Small corrections: WebView in panels needs UXP 6.4+ (the element dates from 6.0, but Premiere starts at UXP 8.1, so this is moot). On macOS the WebView is WKWebView/Safari, so test the bundle in Safari as well as Chromium 99. WebView support inside AE UXP panels is undocumented as of the 27.0 preview. The same bundle runs unchanged only if every host call goes through the HostBridge, which becomes postMessage to the UXP context.

net_effect_on_recommendation:
The core recommendation holds and is slightly strengthened. Ship one CEP 12 multi-host extension (AEFT + PPRO) now, keep an ExtendScript core behind a typed bridge, keep the UI free of host calls, and treat UXP as a later port.

Every load-bearing fact checks out against primary sources:
- AE UXP is early preview only, every API is tagged 27.0, and the public beta is due "by November 2026".
- AE 26.5 is the current release and AE (Beta) is on 27.0.
- CEP is disabled by default in AE/Premiere from December 2028 and gone from versions released from December 2029.
- On 2026-09-29 Adobe staff said there are no plans to remove ExtendScript from Premiere, AE or AME, which settles the vault's "ExtendScript EOL September 2026" error.

Required changes:

1. **The Premiere UXP port is not a simple adapter swap.** As of Premiere 26.5, Premiere UXP cannot read or write MOGRT text or "Graphic Parameters". Adobe acknowledges the gap and targets parity by the end of 2026, with no date (bbb_999 in forum thread 11408). Consequences:
   - Keep Premiere on CEP/ExtendScript, using getMGTComponent, until a Premiere beta build exposes MOGRT component parameters.
   - Put "set MOGRT params" behind a capability check in the HostBridge.
   - Do not commit to a 2027 Premiere UXP move until that ships.
   - Where text editing in Premiere is not needed, consider importAEComps / Dynamic Link instead of MOGRTs, and always pass targetBin (default-bin bug fixed only in 26.5).

2. **Batch MOGRT export is a hypothesis to spike first on AE 26.5, not a settled capability.**
   - exportAsMotionGraphicsTemplate has returned false before finishing since 24.x. Adobe reproduced this on 2024-05-03 and no fix is listed up to 26.5.
   - In premiere-pro-mcp #504 (September 2026), canAddToMotionGraphicsTemplate(comp) returned false for every property on 26.5. It was unresolved, though the reporter never called openInEssentialGraphics.
   - Spike sequence: save → openInEssentialGraphics → canAdd(comp) → addAs(comp, name) → save → export → poll until the file size is stable. Run one export at a time and expect modal warnings.
   - The AE-side plan (.aep import + Essential Properties) does not depend on MOGRT export. If the spike fails, only the Premiere MOGRT path falls back to exporting by hand.

3. **Versions and template rules.**
   - 25.2 stays the hard minimum for reading Essential Property text.
   - Make 26.3+ the tested baseline, because of the 26.2/26.3 Essential Properties fixes and the replaceSource crash fix.
   - Template authors must enable the Source Text font/size/style toggles by hand wherever overrides are needed; this cannot be done by script.
   - Check which 25.x build of AE 2025 is installed on the team's machines.

4. **Distribution.** The "outside the Marketplace is not affected" sentence covers only Marketplace submission cutoffs. An internal signed ZXP is still disabled by default from December 2028 (users must re-enable) and absent from versions released from December 2029. Adobe itself calls CEP unreliable, so finish the AE UXP port during 2027–2028 as planned.

5. **Minor corrections.**
   - Erin Finnegan's caution about CEP UIs was qualified, and her "don't wait" advice pointed to scripts and C++ plug-ins.
   - The AE UXP binding has more differences from ExtendScript than the research listed; for example, a failed add-to-EGP returns undefined instead of false.
   - WebView inside AE UXP panels is undocumented.
   - On macOS the WebView is Safari-based, so test the bundle in Safari as well as Chromium 99.
